mistake.label: THE MISTAKE
mistake.text: "Hi sir, just checking in. Any update?"
mistake.vo: Hi sir, just checking in, any update? That's not a follow-up. That's a reminder that you want something.

fix.label: SAY THIS INSTEAD
fix.text: "Sir, I found *one idea* for your new outlet. *2 minutes?*"
fix.vo: Sir, I found one idea for your new outlet. Can I show you in two minutes?

why.label: WHY IT WORKS
why.text: Every follow-up must *give* something. Then they *wait* for your next call.
why.vo: Every follow-up should give something new. Then the customer waits for your next call.

cta.share: Send this to a teammate who "just checks in" every week.
cta.ask: if you'll try this on your next call
cta.vo: Save this. And send it to a teammate who just checks in every week.

caption:
Stop saying "just checking in." It tells the customer you want something, and gives them nothing.

Top salespeople bring one new useful thing to every follow-up: an idea, a fact, a solution for their goal. Then the customer starts waiting for your call.

SAVE this for your next follow-up.
Send it to a teammate who "just checks in" every week.

Comment VALUE if you'll try this on your next call.

#TheMarketingGuru #SalesTips #FollowUp #SalesTraining #FieldSales
first_comment: What's the most useful thing you've ever brought to a follow-up call?
